info.name: ECommerce - Requirement 5 (scaling)
info.description:
Fifth requirement: three Laravel instances behind one nginx load balancer, shared MySQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, inventory service and web client. The API is the /api/v4/sync and /api/v4/async API of requirement 4, reached through nginx on baseUrl.
Every response carries X-Served-By with the name of the instance that served it. The folder 'Requirement 5 - Scaling and load distribution' proves that the instances are interchangeable.
Order of use: run 02. Login (admin) and 03. Login (user), then run the last folder, then open the Collection Runner on the folder and run it with 30 iterations to see the distribution.

request.description: Creates an account with the role 'user'. Throttled: 10/min per IP.
After LOGIN_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) consecutive wrong passwords the account is locked for LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES (default 15) and returns 423. Also throttled at 10 requests/min per email+IP (429).
Returns a fresh token; the old one is invalidated.
Needs users.view.
Self, or users.view.
Admin only. Optional role: admin or user (default user).
Self: name/email only. users.update: also password and is_active. You cannot manage a user with higher privileges than yours.
Needs users.delete. Not yourself, not the last admin.
Clears a login lockout. Needs users.update.
Admin only. Adds a role to the user.
Admin only. Removes the role from the user.
Admin only. Lowercase letters, digits, - and _.
Admin only. admin and user cannot be renamed.
Admin only. Not allowed for admin/user or a role assigned to users.
Any logged-in user. Filters: search, category, in_stock, per_page.
Distinct product categories.
Admin only. Send as form-data to upload an image.
Admin only. POST with _method=PUT so an image can be uploaded. Plain JSON PUT also works without an image.
Admin only. Removes the product and its image.
Current user cart with totals. The cart is stored in the application cache for 7 days.
Adds a product, or increases its quantity. Rejected when it exceeds the stock.
Sets the quantity of a product already in the cart.
Removes one product from the cart.
Empties the cart.
Turns the cart into an order, reduces the stock, and clears the cart.
Admin only. Filters: status, user_id, per_page.
Orders of the current user only.
Creates an order directly and reduces the stock.
Owner or admin.
Admin only. Statuses: pending, confirmed, processing, delivered, cancelled.
Owner or admin. Restores the stock. Not allowed once delivered or cancelled.
Admin only.
The response carries X-Processing-Mode. It must equal the mode in the path.
Run once with mode=sync and once with mode=async and compare the response time shown by Postman. In async the confirmation mail and the live events are queued, so the response does not wait for them.
Authorizes the private channel of the logged-in user. Replace 1 with the user id. Expected 200 with an auth signature.
Expected 200 for an administrator and 403 for a regular user.
Expected 403 for every user except the owner.
Clears instanceCounts. The load balancer answers ok without reaching an instance.

Run 02. Login (admin) first. Send it repeatedly (Collection Runner, 30 iterations on this one request). X-Served-By changes between app1, app2 and app3. The upstream address chosen by nginx is in X-Upstream.

exec: pm.test('the load balancer reports the upstream', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Upstream')).to.be.a('string'));
const total = Object.values(counts).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
pm.test('requests reached more than one instance', () => pm.expect(Object.keys(counts).length).to.be.above(1));

request.description: The token is valid on every instance because all of them share the same JWT secret.
Starts the cart check from an empty cart.
Adds two units of product 1 and remembers the instance that served the request.
The cart added through one instance is shown by whichever instance answers now, because the cart lives in the shared Redis.

exec: pm.test('the cart shows the added item', () => pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('the quantity is the one that was added', () => pm.expect(String(items[0].quantity)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('expectedQuantity')));

request.description: A different instance changes the cart.
Shows the change made by another instance.
In async mode the mail job goes to the emails queue and one of the three workers takes it.

item.name: 11. RabbitMQ - emails queue has three workers

request.description: The management API reports how many consumers read the queue. With the compose file there are three workers.

item.name: 12. RabbitMQ - broadcasts queue has three workers

request.description: Same check for the broadcasts queue.
Needs the mail profile and MAIL_MAILER=smtp. Each order produces one mail per recipient, never two.

Set the collection variable stoppedInstance to the stopped instance (for example app2) and run this request several times. Requests keep succeeding and are answered by the other instances. Clear the variable afterwards.

exec: pm.test('the stopped instance did not answer', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Served-By')).to.not.eql(stopped));
pm.test('processing mode header matches the path', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Processing-Mode')).to.eql(mode));
